scan.summary: This is Oregon DEQ's air permit for the Portland facility. It covers the acid and caustic repackaging scrubbers and the four solvent tanks vented to a carbon unit. Because it is the agency's own document, there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is meeting its conditions and renewing it in time. It expires November 15, 2026, 49 days from today, and both possible renewal-application deadlines have already passed. The most urgent question is whether a complete renewal application was filed on time. If it was not, the permit ends on its expiration date and the scrubbed and vented sources cannot legally run after that.
scan.freshness_note: This is the version issued September 1, 2021, and it is still in force until November 15, 2026. Ask for three things: a copy of the renewal application you submitted and proof DEQ received it (date-stamped submission or a Your DEQ Online confirmation), any letter from DEQ saying the application is complete, and any renewed permit or draft permit DEQ has issued. If no renewal was filed, contact DEQ Northwest Region right away, before November 15, 2026.

conditions.title: Operate the permitted sources in line with all permit conditions and all applicable DEQ rules
conditions.evidence_expected: The full set of records listed below. No separate document is needed.

conditions.title: Do not run the permitted sources after November 15, 2026 without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application
conditions.evidence_expected: A renewed permit, or proof that a timely and complete renewal application was filed

conditions.title: Submit a complete renewal application no later than 120 days before expiration, which the permit gives as on or before July 18, 2026. The current rule sets 180 days for Standard permits; see the confidence notes.
conditions.evidence_expected: A copy of the renewal application, with a submission receipt or Your DEQ Online confirmation dated on or before the deadline

conditions.title: Give DEQ written notice at least 60 days before any change in ownership, and before any change to a permitted source that would increase emissions
conditions.evidence_expected: Copies of notice letters sent to DEQ, or a note on file that no ownership change or emission-increasing change has happened

conditions.title: Operate scrubbers S-1 (acid line) and S-2 (caustic line), and tanks T-3 to T-6 vented to carbon unit C-1, as described
conditions.evidence_expected: An equipment list matching the permit. Scrubber design flows are 4,500 scfm and 3,000 scfm; the tanks are 10,000 gallons each with fixed roofs.

conditions.title: Keep pressure drop across S-1 and S-2 between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column while each line runs, and record a reading once per operating day
conditions.evidence_expected: A scrubber log with a daily pressure-drop entry for each scrubber on every operating day, with out-of-range readings marked

conditions.title: Inspect each scrubber's recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing and mist eliminator at least once per calendar quarter, recording the date, the inspector and any corrective action
conditions.evidence_expected: Quarterly inspection entries in the scrubber log for S-1 and S-2

conditions.title: Check the C-1 outlet with a detector tube weekly. Replace the carbon at least every 12 months, or sooner if breakthrough is detected, and record each replacement.
conditions.evidence_expected: A weekly detector-tube check log, carbon change-out records or vendor invoices, and spent-carbon disposal paperwork

conditions.title: Keep visible emissions at or below 20% opacity, except for periods adding up to no more than three minutes in any hour
conditions.evidence_expected: Visible-emission observation records if you keep them, and records of any opacity events

conditions.title: Submit an annual report by February 15 covering the previous calendar year: throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon replacement dates and excess emission events
conditions.evidence_expected: Copies of each annual report and proof of submission

conditions.title: Submit a semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
conditions.evidence_expected: Copies of each semi-annual report and proof of submission, including the one due July 31, 2026

conditions.title: Keep all records required by the permit for at least five years and make them available to DEQ on request
conditions.evidence_expected: An organized archive of scrubber logs, carbon records and reports going back five years

conditions.title: During a scrubber malfunction, take reasonable steps to minimize emissions, including stopping the associated repackaging line until the scrubber is back in service
conditions.evidence_expected: Malfunction and shutdown records, and a written procedure telling operators to stop the line

conditions.title: Notify DEQ by phone or email within 24 hours of discovering any deviation, then send a written report within 15 days covering cause, duration and corrective action
conditions.evidence_expected: A deviation log, copies of 24-hour notices and 15-day written reports

conditions.title: Pay the annual permit fee DEQ invoices, by the due date on the invoice
conditions.evidence_expected: DEQ fee invoices and proof of payment

scan.confidence_notes: I am sure of everything I read: the permit number, the issue date (September 1, 2021), the expiration (November 15, 2026), the Portland site address, and each condition. The document is clear and I read all six pages. Where I am less sure: (1) Renewal timing. Condition 1.3 says 120 days (July 18, 2026). The current rule text I found says a Standard ACDP renewal is due <cite index="7-2">180 days prior to the expiration date of a Standard ACDP</cite>, which works out to about May 19, 2026. Both dates have passed, so the practical point is the same: confirm a complete renewal was filed. I cannot tell from here which deadline DEQ would hold you to. It may depend on the rule in effect when the permit was issued. (2) What happens if nothing was filed. Under OAR 340-216-0082 a permit ends automatically on <cite index="10-3,10-4">failure to submit a timely and complete application for permit renewal or reassignment as required in OAR 340-216-0040. Termination is effective on the permit expiration date</cite>. A 2025 DEQ enforcement case against another company shows DEQ does act on this. (3) I found no gaps because a permit is the agency's own document. I have not checked whether the company is actually meeting any condition. That depends on records not provided here. (4) Facts about tank contents and what other rules they trigger are inferred from the equipment list, not read.

STATE OF OREGON
DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY
Northwest Region · 700 NE Multnomah Street, Suite 600, Portland, Oregon
97232
STANDARD AIR CONTAMINANT DISCHARGE PERMIT
Issued under OAR 340-216
Permit number: 26-2841-ST-01
Permittee: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC
Facility: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, Portland Facility
Facility address: 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Source category: Chemical storage and repackaging with vapor control
Date issued: September 1, 2021
Expiration date: November 15, 2026
This permit is issued in accordance with the provisions of ORS 468A.040 and OAR 340-216 and
authorizes the permittee to operate the air contaminant sources described below at the facility address,
subject to the conditions of this permit.
SECTION 1. GENERAL CONDITIONS
1.1 The permittee shall operate the sources listed in Section 2 in compliance with all conditions of this
permit and all applicable rules of the Department.
1.2 This permit expires on November 15, 2026. Operation of the permitted sources after the expiration
date without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application is a violation of this permit.
1.3 The permittee shall submit a complete application for renewal of this permit no later than 120 days
before the expiration date, that is, on or before July 18, 2026. A permittee that submits a timely and
complete renewal application may continue to operate under the terms of this permit until the Department
takes final action on the application.
1.4 The permittee shall notify the Department in writing at least 60 days before any change in ownership,
and before any modification to a permitted source that would increase emissions of any regulated
pollutant.
SECTION 2. PERMITTED SOURCES
2.1 Packed-bed wet scrubber S-1 serving the acid repackaging line (design flow 4,500 scfm).
2.2 Packed-bed wet scrubber S-2 serving the caustic repackaging line (design flow 3,000 scfm).
2.3 Solvent storage tanks T-3, T-4, T-5 and T-6 (each 10,000 gallons, fixed roof, vented to carbon
adsorption unit C-1).
SECTION 3. OPERATING AND MONITORING CONDITIONS
3.1 The permittee shall maintain the pressure drop across each scrubber S-1 and S-2 within the range of
2.0 to 6.0 inches of water column whenever the associated line is operating, and shall record the pressure
drop reading once per operating day in a scrubber log.
3.2 The permittee shall inspect each scrubber's recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing and mist
eliminator at least once per calendar quarter and record the date, the inspector and any corrective action in
the scrubber log.
3.3 The permittee shall replace the carbon in adsorption unit C-1 at least once every 12 months or when
breakthrough is detected by the weekly detector-tube check at the C-1 outlet, whichever comes first, and
shall record each replacement.
3.4 Visible emissions from any permitted source shall not exceed 20 percent opacity for any period
aggregating more than three minutes in any one hour.
SECTION 4. RECORDKEEPING AND REPORTING
4.1 The permittee shall submit an annual report to the Department by February 15 of each year covering
the previous calendar year, including total throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon
replacement dates and any excess emission events.
4.2 The permittee shall submit a semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
of the same year.
4.3 The permittee shall keep all records required by this permit for at least five years from the date of the
record and make them available to the Department on request.
SECTION 5. EXCESS EMISSIONS AND UPSETS
5.1 The permittee shall take all reasonable steps to minimize emissions during any period of scrubber
malfunction, including stopping the associated repackaging line until the scrubber is returned to service.
5.2 The permittee shall notify the Department by telephone or email within 24 hours of discovering any
deviation from a condition of this permit, and shall submit a written report within 15 days describing the
deviation, its cause, its duration and the corrective action taken.
SECTION 6. ADMINISTRATIVE
6.1 This permit may be modified, suspended or revoked for cause, including violation of any condition,
obtaining the permit by misrepresentation, or a change in any condition that requires reduction of the
permitted emissions.
6.2 The permittee shall pay the annual permit fee invoiced by the Department by the due date stated on
the invoice.
